title: PowerToys Run - System.InvalidOperationException: Cyclic reference found while evaluating the Style property on element

fix_assessment.rationale: Current 0.102.3001 reports and the WPF system-theme stack align with PowerToys Run's runtime ThemeMode and custom resource-dictionary updates. PR #47367 proposed a focused correction but is closed unmerged; the exact cause still needs a current-build reproduction.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep PowerToys Run's runtime theme resources on one update path
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: WPF's Fluent theme manager continues to react to system theme changes while PowerToys Run replaces window resource dictionaries for high-contrast themes, allowing style invalidation to revisit a cyclic resource reference. The reported stack and current code path fit, but the failure has not been reliably reproduced.
plan: Reassess the final changes in closed, unmerged PR #47367 against current main rather than treating that PR as a shipped fix.

Preserve Fluent static resources during window initialization, then avoid simultaneous WPF ThemeMode and custom high-contrast dictionary ownership at runtime; remove custom high-contrast dictionaries before restoring Light or Dark mode.
Add regression coverage for Light/Dark and High Contrast transitions, including a test that exercises the actual window resource update rather than only mapping Theme values.
verification: Reproduce on the reported Windows 11 x64 build while PowerToys Run is open, then verify the cyclic-reference exception no longer occurs during repeated system-theme transitions.
Exercise entering and leaving High Contrast and verify the intended Fluent/custom resources and accessibility colors remain available.
Build and run the focused PowerToys Run tests; an enum-to-ThemeMode unit test alone does not validate resource-dictionary transitions.

confidence.rationale: The current report provides the exact WPF system-theme stack, current main contains the matching theme/resource updates, and the final PR diff targets that path; no reliable reproduction or merged fix proves causality.

issue_context.summary: PowerToys Run continues to report a WPF cyclic-style-reference exception during system-theme processing on 0.102.3001.0; the proposed PR fix is not in current main.
known_information: The November 3 report identifies PowerToys 0.102.3001.0, Windows 11 build 10.0.26300, x64, the exact cyclic-reference exception, and a stack through ThemeManager.OnSystemThemeChanged, AddOrUpdateThemeResources, and SystemThemeFilterMessage: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/36451#issuecomment-6600083891
The reporter attached a PowerToys diagnostic archive but says no reliable reproduction scenario is known.
Earlier reports include a Windows light-to-dark change and an Auto Dark Mode report; the latter's NullReferenceException is a separate symptom and is not treated as proof of this root cause.
PR #47367 is closed, remains a draft, and has no merge commit. Its final diff changed PowerToys Run's startup/runtime ThemeMode and high-contrast resource handling.
Current upstream main still includes the Fluent application theme dictionary and the runtime ThemeManager path that applies Light/Dark ThemeMode while replacing custom high-contrast dictionaries.
inferences: A conflict between WPF's system-theme resource update and PowerToys Run's custom high-contrast resources is a plausible cause, not a confirmed one.
The final changes in PR #47367 are a useful candidate direction, but they require review and transition-level regression coverage before being treated as a fix.
issue_context.analysis: The latest report is a current, concrete recurrence with a stack that points to WPF's system-theme resource update, and the commenter explicitly asks about PR #47367. That PR is closed and unmerged, and the relevant change is absent from current main. This supports a focused, confidence-scored design direction, but not a claim that the PR was released or that its hypothesis is proven. Reproduce the system/high-contrast transition on a current build before implementation.
initial_investigation: Read the current issue body and latest comments, including the November 3 current-version report, its exact stack, attached-report reference, and statement that no reliable reproduction is known.

Checked PR #47367's current state and final diff; it is closed, draft, and unmerged. The candidate adds a high-contrast ThemeMode.None path, preserves startup Fluent resources with a compatible fallback, and clears custom high-contrast dictionaries when returning to standard themes.
Fetched current upstream main ThemeManager.cs and App.xaml; confirmed the candidate high-contrast handling is not present and the Fluent dictionary remains loaded.
Inspected PowerLauncher.Helper.ThemeManager.SetSystemTheme: it sets Application.Current.ThemeMode and clears/adds custom high-contrast ResourceDictionaries on the runtime update path.
Kept the October 29 NullReferenceException report separate from the cyclic-reference defect rather than merging distinct exception types.

judgment.rationale: The current-version stack, source path, and unmerged targeted PR provide enough evidence for one focused design direction. The exact trigger remains unknown, so a maintainer reproduction action and yellow confidence are retained.
evidence: The November 3 report confirms the cyclic-reference exception on 0.102.3001.0 and Windows 11 x64 build 10.0.26300, with the WPF system-theme resource stack: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/36451#issuecomment-6600083891
The reporter explicitly says a reliable reproduction scenario is not known.
PR #47367, the proposed fix cited by the reporter, is closed and unmerged; current main does not contain its high-contrast ThemeMode/resource changes.
Current PowerToys Run source updates Application.Current.ThemeMode and custom high-contrast dictionaries through SetSystemTheme, matching the reported system-theme path.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the system/high-contrast transition on a current build, then review the focused theme-resource design rather than assuming PR #47367 shipped.

actions.label: Reproduce system-theme transition in PowerToys Run

reproduce.title: Exercise PowerToys Run during Windows theme transitions
reproduce.version_requirement: First test PowerToys 0.102.3001.0 on Windows 11 x64 build 10.0.26300, then compare with a current build.
prerequisites: Use a disposable Windows profile or VM with PowerToys Run available.
Keep PowerToys Run open while changing the Windows system theme.
setup: Capture the exact PowerToys and Windows versions and the selected PowerToys Run theme.
If testing Auto Dark Mode, record it as a separate trigger; do not treat its reported NullReferenceException as the same failure.
steps: Launch PowerToys Run and leave it open while switching Windows Settings > Personalization > Colors from Light to Dark and back.
Repeat with Windows High Contrast enabled and then disabled, recording whether the failure requires entering or leaving High Contrast.
If an exception appears, capture its timestamp and full stack with a fresh /bugreport and compare it with the reported ThemeManager.OnSystemThemeChanged path.
reproduce.expected_result: Repeated theme transitions complete without a cyclic-style-reference exception; any failure is tied to a specific transition and captured stack.

summary: Current-version cyclic-reference report aligns with PowerToys Run's theme-resource path; PR #47367 is an unmerged candidate, not a shipped fix.
next_action: Reproduce the current system/high-contrast theme transition and review the focused resource-ownership design.
